questions.statement: You wear it on your upper body. It has buttons. What is it?
questions.context: Mateo se alista para el colegio en Bogotá y se pone la camisa del uniforme.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A 'skirt' hangs from the waist; it is not for the upper body.
Incorrect. 'Shoes' go on your feet, not on your upper body.
Incorrect. 'Socks' go on your feet and have no buttons.
Correct. A 'shirt' goes on your upper body and often has buttons.

questions.explanation:
'Shirt' es camisa. Las pistas son la parte del cuerpo (arriba, el torso) y los botones. 'Shoes' y 'socks' van en los pies y 'skirt' (falda) va de la cintura hacia abajo.

questions.statement: You wear them on your feet when you walk to school. What are they?
questions.context: Antes de salir de la casa en Cali, Sara busca lo que se pone en los pies.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A 'hat' goes on your head.
Correct. You wear 'shoes' on your feet to walk.
Incorrect. A 'jacket' goes over your shirt, on your upper body.
Incorrect. A 'skirt' goes from the waist down, not on the feet.

questions.explanation:
'Shoes' son zapatos y se usan en los pies ('feet'). 'Hat' va en la cabeza, 'jacket' sobre la camisa y 'skirt' es una falda.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "It is very sunny. Put on your ___ to protect your head."
questions.context: Hace mucho sol en Cartagena y la mamá de Andrés le recuerda protegerse la cabeza.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'Socks' go on your feet, not on your head.
Correct. A 'hat' goes on your head and protects it from the sun.
Incorrect. A 'skirt' cannot protect your head.
Incorrect. 'Gloves' go on your hands.

questions.explanation:
'Hat' es sombrero o gorra. La oración dice 'to protect your head' (para proteger tu cabeza), y la única prenda que va en la cabeza es 'hat'.

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "Mariana wears a ___ to the party. It is one piece of clothing from her shoulders to her knees."
questions.context: Mariana se viste para la fiesta de cumpleaños de su prima en Medellín.

options.feedback: Correct. A 'dress' is one piece of clothing that covers the body from the shoulders down.
Incorrect. 'Pants' cover only the legs, and the word is plural: 'a pants' is wrong.
Incorrect. A 'cap' goes on the head.
Incorrect. 'Boots' go on the feet, and 'a boots' is wrong because it is plural.

questions.explanation:
'Dress' es vestido: una sola prenda que va de los hombros hacia abajo. 'Pants' (pantalón) solo cubre las piernas, 'cap' (gorra) va en la cabeza y 'boots' (botas) en los pies.

questions.statement:
Read: "In Bogotá it is cold in the morning. Juan wears long pants, a sweater and a jacket."
What does Juan wear on his legs?
questions.context: Juan vive en Bogotá, donde las mañanas suelen ser frías.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A 'sweater' goes on the upper body, not on the legs.
Incorrect. A 'jacket' goes over the sweater, on the upper body.
Incorrect. The text does not mention shorts; Juan wears long pants because it is cold.
Correct. 'Pants' are worn on the legs, and the text says 'long pants'.

questions.explanation:
En el texto Juan usa tres prendas. 'Long pants' (pantalón largo) es la que va en las piernas; 'sweater' y 'jacket' van en la parte de arriba del cuerpo.

questions.statement:
Read the dialogue.
Mom: "It's cold. Put on your ___ before your shoes."
Pablo: "OK, Mom!"
questions.context: Una mañana fría en Tunja, la mamá de Pablo le ayuda a vestirse.

options.feedback: Correct. You put on 'socks' before your shoes to keep your feet warm.
Incorrect. A 'hat' goes on your head, and you do not put it on before your shoes.
Incorrect. A 'T-shirt' goes on your upper body; the order with shoes does not matter.
Incorrect. A 'skirt' is not something you put on before your shoes.

questions.explanation:
'Socks' son medias. Se ponen antes de los zapatos ('before your shoes') y abrigan los pies. Las otras prendas no se relacionan con ponerse los zapatos.

questions.statement:
Read: "Laura goes to the beach in Santa Marta. It is very hot."
Which clothes are best for Laura?
questions.context: Laura viaja con su familia a la playa de Santa Marta en vacaciones.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A jacket and gloves are for cold weather, not for a very hot beach.
Incorrect. A sweater and boots keep you warm; they are not good for a hot day.
Correct. Shorts and a T-shirt are light clothes for hot weather.
Incorrect. A scarf and a coat are winter clothes.

questions.explanation:
Para elegir la ropa hay que mirar el clima: 'very hot' significa que hace mucho calor. 'Shorts and a T-shirt' (pantaloneta y camiseta) son prendas frescas; las otras opciones son para el frío.

questions.context: En la clase de inglés de Bucaramanga, los niños describen la ropa de sus compañeros.

options.feedback: Incorrect. With 'she' the verb needs -s: 'she wears'.
Incorrect. After 'a' the noun is singular: 'a red skirt'.
Incorrect. The color goes before the noun: 'a red skirt', not before the verb.
Correct. 'She wears' has the -s, and 'a red skirt' is singular with the color before the noun.

questions.explanation: En inglés, con 'she' el verbo lleva -s ('wears'), después de 'a' el sustantivo va en singular ('skirt') y el color va antes de la prenda: 'a red skirt' (una falda roja).
